1	# Quality gates
2	
3	## Anti-rationalization
4	
5	These are excuses agents (and humans) reach for when they want to skip a gate. Each pairs with the reality that makes the excuse wrong. Read this section before relaxing any rule below.
6	
7	| Rationalization | Reality |
8	|---|---|
9	| "This is too small for the spec / phase model" | The phase model is what makes 'small' verifiable. Skipping produces work that cannot be approved. |
10	| "I'll add the phase-approval artifact later" | Without it, the next agent has no audit trail and the loop cannot advance. The artifact *is* the gate. |
11	| "I can just quickly implement this" | Audit-first exists because existing code may already satisfy the goal. Re-implementing without auditing produces drift. |
12	| "The test isn't strictly necessary here" | The testing gate requires a test that would fail if the change were reverted. If you can't write one, you don't understand the change. |
13	| "Two near-duplicates is fine for now" | The DRY gate targets logic that encodes the same invariant in two places. That kind of duplication silently rots when one side changes. |
14	| "I'll skip the planner — the design is obvious" | The planning gate exists for changes that cross layers, touch persistence/auth, or have multiple plausible strategies. 'Obvious' is what missed-the-tradeoff sounds like before review. |
15	| "I'll loosen project settings just for this run" | Project settings are shared. Permissive execution belongs in `settings.local.json` or CLI flags, never committed. |
16	| "Code review can wait until after merge" | The review gate catches duplication, missed drift, and architecture violations the implementer is least likely to see. After-merge review is a documentation step, not a gate. |
17	| "I'll push anyway, CI will catch it" | CI is shared infrastructure. Broken master pages humans, blocks deploys, and disrupts other consumers of the loop. The pre-commit verify gate exists so easy classes of failure are caught locally. |
18	| "I'll skip the verification sprint — nothing changed there" | Cumulative regressions are the failure mode the sprint exists to catch. 'Nothing changed' is an assumption, not evidence. |
19	| "Discovered work can wait for a later phase" | Discovered work that blocks the current phase is part of the current phase. Deferring it produces phases that pass review but don't actually deliver. |
20	
21	If you find yourself making one of these arguments, stop and re-read the relevant gate below.
22	
23	## Universal gate
24	A phase is only complete when all of the following are true:
25	- documented acceptance criteria pass
26	- relevant tests pass
27	- `code-reviewer` approves
28	- `qa-playwright` approves for user-visible or browser-based work
29	- docs are updated for any rule or architecture decision
30	- `artifacts/phase-approval.json` is written with `approved: true`
31	- the outer orchestration layer creates a git commit before the next phase begins
32	
33	## Testing gate
34	A phase is not complete unless:
35	- every new module, endpoint, or public behavior has at least one test exercising its primary path
36	- every bug fix includes a regression test that would fail without the fix
37	- tests are written before or alongside implementation code, not retrofitted after
38	- test names describe the behavior under test, not implementation details
39	- edge cases and error paths are tested for any logic identified as risky in the spec or decision memo
40	
41	When coverage tooling is available in the target project, aim for meaningful branch coverage of new code. Do not pursue a numeric target at the expense of test quality — a focused test that catches real regressions is worth more than broad shallow coverage.
42	
43	"Relevant tests pass" (from the universal gate) means: tests exist that would fail if the feature were removed or the bug fix reverted.
44	
45	### Browser-API limitations (Phase 2b + Phase 6)
46	
47	Some browser APIs cannot be exercised reliably under jsdom or headless Playwright in this project's test environment. Each affected phase declares a scoped concession.
48	
49	**Phase 2b** — `RTCPeerConnection` / WebRTC DataChannel, `navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia`, and `DeviceMotionEvent`:
50	
51	- **Pure-logic modules** (peer state machine, wire format, motion impulse detection, calibration math) remain fully unit-tested under vitest with stubbed browser APIs. These tests gate the testing-gate's "would fail if reverted" rule.
52	- **Transport handshake and live sensor input** are gated by a per-sub-phase manual real-device QA script (`app/verify-phase-2b{1,2,3,4}.mjs`) — same pattern as the existing `verify-phase{4,5}.mjs` flows.
53	- Each Phase 2b sub-phase approval artifact must include a `manual_qa` field naming the device used and the steps performed; without it, the phase is not approved.
54	
55	**Phase 6** — HTML5 `<video>` element semantics (`play()`, `currentTime` write, `timeupdate`), `requestVideoFrameCallback`, and live `navigator.storage.estimate()` behavior:
56	
57	- **Pure-logic modules** (`clipmode/library.ts` metadata extraction with stubbed `<video>`, `clipmode/runner.ts` state machine with manual `currentTime` advance, `clipmode/random.ts` distribution sampler, Dexie blob round-trip via `fake-indexeddb`, the typed `addClip()` quota / size / type result branches) remain fully unit-tested. These tests gate the testing-gate's "would fail if reverted" rule.
58	- **HTML5 `<video>` semantics and `requestVideoFrameCallback`** are gated by a per-sub-phase manual real-device QA script (`app/verify-phase6-{1,2,3}.mjs`). Specifically: the ±33 ms cue-shown precision criterion (6.3), the scrub-to-1-frame precision criterion (6.2), and the end-to-end clip-import → tag → drill → summary flow are MANUAL.
59	- **Browser-version gate** — Clip mode is feature-detected via `requestVideoFrameCallback`. Browsers without it (Safari < 15.4) cannot enable Clip mode; this is intentional to avoid measurement-system incoherence given the spec's 450 ms hesitation / 600 ms late thresholds.

62	This is a scoped concession, not a general gate relaxation. See `artifacts/decision-memo.md` §B2 (Phase 2b) and §B5–§B6 (Phase 6) for the full reasoning.

64	## DRY and reuse gate
65	- business rules and validation logic must exist in exactly one place
66	- if the same logic appears in more than one layer, extract it to a shared module or justify the duplication in a decision memo
67	- builders must check for existing utilities and shared modules before creating new ones
68	- code-reviewer must reject changes that introduce unjustified duplication
69	
70	## Drift detection gate
71	Before starting a new implementation phase, the assigned builder must:
72	- review code produced in prior phases for overlap with the current task
73	- flag any inconsistency between the current plan and already-approved code
74	- prefer extending existing modules over creating parallel implementations
75	- report discovered drift as a blocking issue for project-lead to resolve before proceeding
76	
77	## Verification sprint gate
78	Before starting a phase that builds on a completed user-visible or end-to-end foundation, run a full verification of the cumulative system to confirm prior work still functions:
79	- run the complete test suite (unit, integration, and browser/E2E when applicable)
80	- exercise the primary user workflow end-to-end via `qa-playwright` for browser projects, or via the project's domain-equivalent QA (CLI smoke test, integration harness) for non-browser projects
81	- fix any regressions before starting new work — do not layer new complexity onto broken foundations
82	- record verification results under a `verification_sprint` field in the next `artifacts/phase-approval.json`
83	
84	## Planning gate
85	Use a planning and adversarial review cycle before implementation when any of the following are true:
86	- the change crosses multiple layers
87	- persistence or schema choices are involved
88	- auth, security, or public internet exposure is involved
89	- the refactor could invalidate prior assumptions
90	- there are at least two plausible implementation strategies
91	- scaffold control flow, capability generation, or packaging behavior is affected (self-improvement mode)
92	
93	Required outputs:
94	- `artifacts/decision-memo.md`
95	- optional ADR in `docs/adr/` (use `docs/ADR_TEMPLATE.md`; follow naming convention `ADR-NNNN-short-title.md`)
96	
97	## Meta-project gates
98	For scaffold self-improvement work, a phase is not complete until:
99	- the current meta-phase acceptance criteria pass
100	- `strategy-planner` is used for material design changes
101	- `architecture-red-team` is used for architectural or autonomy-affecting changes
102	- `code-reviewer` approves
103	- generated skills validate and package successfully for any skill-related phase
104	- docs and manifest entries are updated

119	must include:
120	- rationale
121	- tradeoffs
122	- rollback path
123	- updated docs
124	- explicit reviewer approval
125	
126	## Commit gate
127	Claude must stop after writing `artifacts/phase-approval.json`.
128	The host-side wrapper is responsible for:
129	1. reading the approval artifact
130	2. running the pre-commit verification gate (see below)
131	3. creating a git commit
132	4. resuming Claude for the next phase
133	
134	## Pre-commit verification gate
135	The wrapper runs a project-defined fast-check command before creating any phase commit, regardless of whether `AUTO_PUSH` is enabled. Mechanism lives in the scaffold (`scripts/run-until-done.sh`); policy lives in the project (`scripts/phasekit-verify.sh`).
136	
137	Scope of the verify command:
138	- fast checks only — lint, typecheck, formatter, unit tests
139	- **not** full E2E or integration suites (those belong to the verification-sprint gate, which Claude drives at phase boundaries)
140	- target under ~30 seconds; this runs every iteration
141	
142	On failure:
143	- the commit is **not** created
144	- the wrapper writes `artifacts/phase-verify-failed.json` with the failing command, exit code, attempt counter, and a tail of the output
145	- the next iteration's `CONTINUE_PROMPT.txt` directs Claude to fix the failure before doing any new phase work
146	- after `VERIFY_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (default 3) consecutive failures on the same artifact, the wrapper writes `artifacts/phase-blocked.json` and exits so a human can intervene
147	
148	To recover from a circuit-break: fix the underlying failure (or set `VERIFY_SKIP=1` if the next iteration legitimately needs to commit red), then re-run `scripts/run-until-done.sh`. The wrapper resets the verify-attempt counter at the start of any fresh `CLAUDE_MODE=new` run; `phase-blocked.json` is cleared automatically by the iteration's `cleanup_artifacts` step.
149	
150	Escape hatches:
151	- `VERIFY_SKIP=1` bypasses the gate for one iteration (use sparingly — docs-only phases or TDD phases that intentionally commit a red test)
152	- `PHASEKIT_VERIFY_CMD="..."` overrides the script with a one-shot command
153	
154	Configuration is project-owned: edit `scripts/phasekit-verify.sh` (rendered into the project at enrich time) to declare the right fast checks for the stack. Until configured, the gate fail-opens with a warning so un-instrumented projects continue to work.
155	
156	## Suggested phase approval artifact
157	
158	```json
159	{
160	  "phase": "phase-4",
161	  "approved": true,
162	  "summary": "Primary browser workflow verified and accepted.",
163	  "suggested_commit_message": "phase-4: approve browser workflow"
164	}
165	```
166	
167	For phases that required a planning gate, include a `decision_memo` field referencing the governing artifact:
168	
169	```json
170	{
171	  "phase": "meta-M5.1",
172	  "approved": true,
173	  "summary": "...",
174	  "decision_memo": "artifacts/decision-memo.md",
175	  "suggested_commit_message": "meta-M5.1: ..."
176	}
177	```
178	
179	This field is optional for phases that did not require a planning gate, and required for those that did.
180	
181	## Final completion artifact
182	
183	```json
184	{
185	  "done": true,
186	  "summary": "Required phases completed and production requirements satisfied.",
187	  "final_notes": [
188	    "Known limitation 1",
189	    "Known limitation 2"
190	  ]
191	}
192	```
193	
194	## Discovered work and phase expansion
195	
196	During execution, the lead may discover that the current phase is underspecified or that additional prerequisite work is required.
197	
198	In that case:
199	
200	### Minor discovered work
201	If the new work is small, backward-compatible, and does not require external input:
202	- update the relevant docs directly
203	- append or refine acceptance criteria
204	- continue the current phase without asking the user
205	
206	### Major but self-resolvable discovered work
207	If the new work is substantial but can be resolved using existing repo context and subagents:
208	- invoke strategy-planner and architecture-red-team as needed
209	- update META_SPEC.md, META_PHASES.md, ADRs, or related docs
210	- split the phase into subphases or append follow-on phases as needed
211	- do not ask the user for confirmation merely to continue planning
212	- write `artifacts/phase-update.json` if the phase plan changed materially
213	
214	### External blocker
215	If required information is genuinely missing from the repo and cannot be resolved autonomously:
216	- write `artifacts/phase-blocked.json`
217	- stop without writing `artifacts/phase-approval.json`
218	
219	Approved phase numbering must remain stable. Do not renumber already-approved phases retroactively.

2	 * Pure helpers for ClipTagScreen — frame-step math and clamping.
3	 *
4	 * Per the Phase 6 decision memo §2 "Tagging UX": the −1 frame / +1 frame
5	 * buttons step by `1/30 s` (≈33.33 ms). We do not know the source clip's
6	 * FPS, but this is "good enough for tagging at human reaction-time
7	 * resolution" — the ±33 ms cue-shown precision criterion lives in Phase
8	 * 6.3 (drill mode), not here.

10	 * Scrub-to-1-frame precision is a MANUAL gate per `docs/QUALITY_GATES.md`

12	 * below are the unit-testable surface.

15	/** Frame step in milliseconds: 1/30 s ≈ 33.33 ms. */
16	export const FRAME_STEP_MS = 1000 / 30
17	
18	/**
19	 * Returns the new tag position after stepping by `delta` frames, clamped
20	 * to `[0, durationMs]`. `delta` is in units of frames (typically ±1).
21	 * Result is rounded to the nearest millisecond.
22	 */
23	export function stepFrame(
24	  currentMs: number,
25	  delta: number,
26	  durationMs: number,
27	): number {
28	  const next = currentMs + delta * FRAME_STEP_MS
29	  return Math.max(0, Math.min(Math.round(next), Math.max(0, durationMs)))
30	}
31	
32	/**
33	 * Clamps a free-form cueAtMs (e.g. from a range-input slider or
34	 * `<video>.currentTime`) to `[0, durationMs]`. Mirrors the clamp used by
35	 * `library.updateClipTag()` so callers can apply the same rule in the UI
36	 * before the persistence layer ever sees the value.
37	 */
38	export function clampCueAtMs(cueAtMs: number, durationMs: number): number {
39	  if (!Number.isFinite(cueAtMs)) return 0
40	  return Math.max(0, Math.min(Math.round(cueAtMs), Math.max(0, durationMs)))
41	}

1	// Phase 6.2 verification driver — clip tagging UI.
2	//
3	// Gate-grade automated checks (run against `npm run dev` on http://localhost:5173):
4	//   C1. From the empty library, the "Tag" button is not shown (no clips yet)
5	//       but the import label is present — sanity check that the row-actions
6	//       toolbar only renders for real rows.
7	//   C2. After seeding one clip directly into Dexie (the headless context
8	//       cannot reliably drive `<input type=file>`-then-`extractDurationMs`
9	//       on synthetic blobs), the clip row exposes a "Tag" button and a
10	//       "needs tag" marker.
11	//   C3. Clicking "Tag" opens ClipTagScreen with the cue-type select
12	//       populated with all 8 CUE_LIBRARY entries, the scrub bar, the +/-1
13	//       frame buttons, the Save button, and the Close button all visible.
14	//   C4. Selecting a cue type ("blitzes") and clicking Save persists; the
15	//       Save indicator appears. Closing back to the library shows the
16	//       "needs tag" marker gone (the clip is now tagged) and re-opening
17	//       the tag screen prefills the cue-select with "blitzes".
18	//
19	// Manual real-device QA — per QUALITY_GATES.md §"Browser-API limitations
20	// (Phase 2b + Phase 6)" §B5: scrub-to-1-frame precision requires real
21	// <video> + a real .mp4 file. Headless chromium does not decode synthesized
22	// blobs reliably.
23	//   M1. Import 2–3 real .mp4 clips via Manage clips.
24	//   M2. Open Tag on one of them. Scrub the native video controls; the
25	//       custom range slider tracks the video's currentTime within one
26	//       frame of resolution.
27	//   M3. Step ±1 frame with the buttons. The video frame visibly advances
28	//       or retreats by approximately 1/30 s.
29	//   M4. Pick a cue type and Save. Reload the page; re-open Tag on the
30	//       same clip. The cue-select is prefilled with the saved cue and
31	//       the scrub bar is parked at the saved cueAtMs.
32	//   M5. Library: the tagged clip no longer shows the "needs tag" marker;
33	//       untagged siblings still do.

54	async function clearIDB(page) {
55	  await page.evaluate(
56	    () =>
57	      new Promise((r) => {
58	        const req = indexedDB.deleteDatabase('pointfight-reactor')
59	        req.onsuccess = () => r()
60	        req.onerror = () => r()
61	        req.onblocked = () => r()
62	      }),

66	// Seed a clip directly into Dexie so the Tag flow can be exercised without
67	// driving the headless file-picker (which cannot meaningfully decode a
68	// synthesized .mp4 anyway — see §B5 manual QA).
69	async function seedClip(page, { name = 'verify.mp4', durationMs = 5000 } = {}) {
70	  // Open without specifying a version so we attach to whatever Dexie set up
71	  // (Dexie internally multiplies its version by 10 — v4 → IDB v40 — so a
72	  // hardcoded version mismatches). The app must have loaded once for the
73	  // `clips` object store to exist.
74	  await page.evaluate(
75	    async ({ name, durationMs }) => {
76	      const dbReq = indexedDB.open('pointfight-reactor')
77	      const db = await new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
78	        dbReq.onsuccess = () => resolve(dbReq.result)
79	        dbReq.onerror = () => reject(dbReq.error)
80	      })
81	      const tx = db.transaction(['clips'], 'readwrite')
82	      const store = tx.objectStore('clips')
83	      const blob = new Blob([new Uint8Array(1024)], { type: 'video/mp4' })
84	      const id = `clip-verify-${Date.now()}`
85	      await new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
86	        const req = store.put({
87	          id,
88	          name,
89	          mimeType: 'video/mp4',
90	          durationMs,
91	          sizeBytes: blob.size,
92	          importedAt: Date.now(),
93	          blob,
94	        })
95	        req.onsuccess = () => resolve()
96	        req.onerror = () => reject(req.error)
97	      })
98	      await new Promise((r) => (tx.oncomplete = r))
99	      db.close()
100	      return id
101	    },
102	    { name, durationMs },
103	  )
104	}

## Phase 6.2 Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

The implementation is largely solid: pure helpers are well-isolated, tests are clear and behavior-focused, library API extension matches existing patterns, lazy-loading + bundle deltas are within budget, 236/236 vitest passes locally, lint + tsc + build clean. But there are two correctness issues in `ClipTagScreen` plus a verification-artifact inconsistency that block approval.

### Blockers

**B1 — Persisted verify artifact contradicts the PR claim** (Universal gate: "qa-playwright approves for user-visible work" + verification-sprint gate)
- `/home/aaron/dev/projects/aaron/pointfight-reactor/artifacts/phase-6-2-verify/results.json` shows `"automated": {}` and `"fatal": "Error: page.waitForSelector: ... browser has been closed ... waiting for locator('[data-testid=\"clip-library-close\"]')"`.
- The PR description states "C1/C2/C3/C4 all PASS; console_errors: 0", but the latest persisted artifact has no automated entries at all. The PNG screenshots from the earlier passing run are still present (12:56), but the JSON (13:00) is from a subsequent failed re-run. The most recent results.json is the source of truth for phase approval — and it shows a fatal.
- Fix: re-run `app/verify-phase6-2.mjs` against a stable `npm run dev` instance and overwrite `results.json` with passing automated entries before approval.

**B2 — Blob URL effect churns on every clip-state replacement, breaking `<video>` mid-tag** (correctness)
- `/home/aaron/dev/projects/aaron/pointfight-reactor/app/src/ui/ClipTagScreen.tsx:38-52` — the effect's dep is `[clip]` (object identity).
- After a Save, line 89 does `setClip(updated)` with a freshly constructed `ClipRecord`. New reference → effect fires → revokes existing URL → creates a new URL → reassigns `videoRef.current.src` imperatively. Result: the `<video>` element reloads and currentTime resets to 0 every time the user saves, even though the underlying blob hasn't changed.
- A correct fix is either (a) gate the effect on `clip.id` (the blob is immutable per id), e.g. `useEffect(..., [clip?.id])`, then derive the blob fetch inside; or (b) don't reassign `setClip(updated)` on save — keep the original ClipRecord and only mirror `cueId`/`cueAtMs` into the existing one.
- This is the kind of bug the user explicitly asked about ("revokeObjectURL guaranteed"). RevokeObjectURL itself is guaranteed (cleanup fires on every dep change and on unmount), but the effect re-running on save is a UX-correctness regression that no test catches.

**B3 — Initial-load effect re-fires on every parent re-render** (correctness; latent)
- `/home/aaron/dev/projects/aaron/pointfight-reactor/app/src/ui/ClipTagScreen.tsx:22-36` — effect dep is `[clipId, onClose]`.
- `/home/aaron/dev/projects/aaron/pointfight-reactor/app/src/App.tsx:75-78` — parent passes a fresh arrow each render: `onClose={() => { setTaggingClipId(null); setView('clips') }}`.
- Currently benign because App rarely re-renders while on the `tag` view, but the latent behavior is: every parent re-render refetches the clip from Dexie and resets local `cueId` / `cueAtMs` state to the persisted values — silently overwriting unsaved edits.
- Fix: either remove `onClose` from the dep array (use a ref pattern), or wrap `onClose` in `useCallback` in `App.tsx`. The first is the smaller change; just dep on `[clipId]` and document why `onClose` is intentionally excluded.

### Should-fix

**S1 — Component test doesn't validate the blob-URL plumbing it stubs**
- `/home/aaron/dev/projects/aaron/pointfight-reactor/app/src/ui/ClipTagScreen.test.tsx:18-21` stubs `URL.createObjectURL`/`revokeObjectURL` but no test asserts they were called, or that `<video>.src` was assigned. After fixing B2, add a test asserting `URL.createObjectURL` is called exactly once per clipId (and that re-rendering parent does not trigger a second call) — that's the regression test for B2.

**S2 — Missing decision memo entry for `@testing-library/react` adoption** (DRY/conventions — first usage in repo)
- This is the project's first component-test surface. Prior phases routed all UI assertions through `app/verify-phaseN.mjs` Playwright scripts (per the spec-driven §B5 concession). Adding `@testing-library/react` + `@testing-library/jest-dom` + `@testing-library/user-event` (3 new devDeps) is a testing-strategy expansion that should be recorded in `artifacts/decision-memo.md` so a future agent doesn't have to reverse-engineer why two parallel UI-test surfaces exist.
- Per `QUALITY_GATES.md` §"Planning gate" (changes that "could invalidate prior assumptions"), a short memo entry is the appropriate artifact. Just append to the existing Phase 6.2 §B5 section.

**S3 — `@testing-library/jest-dom` declared but unused**
- `app/package.json:27` adds `@testing-library/jest-dom`, but `ClipTagScreen.test.tsx` uses neither `toBeInTheDocument()` nor any other jest-dom matcher (it uses `.not.toBeNull()` instead). The dep ships nothing the codebase needs. Either import its matchers in `src/test/setup.ts` and adopt them, or drop the package.

### Nits

**N1 — Stepframe drift on repeated clicks**
- `stepFrame()` rounds *after each step* (line 29 in `tag.ts`), so 30 forward clicks land on ~990 ms instead of 1000 ms. This is acknowledged in the comment block (§B5: "we never know source FPS") and gated to manual QA, so not blocking. But if you want zero accumulated drift, track frame *count* in state and derive ms = `Math.round(frameCount * FRAME_STEP_MS)` on each render.

**N2 — Playwright addition is appropriate, not removable** 
- The user asked whether dropping the testing-library deps would have been cleaner. No — those are the only practical way to test a `.tsx` component under vitest's jsdom env. Conversely, `playwright` as devDep was overdue (already required by 9 verify scripts) — moving it from implicit-via-`npx` to explicit is the right call.

**N3 — data-testid convention compliance**
- All new ids (`clip-tag-loading`, `clip-tag-close`, `clip-tag-video`, `clip-tag-frame-back`, `clip-tag-scrub`, `clip-tag-frame-forward`, `clip-tag-position`, `clip-tag-cue-select`, `clip-tag-save`, `clip-tag-saved`, `clip-tag-open`, `clip-row-actions`, `clip-needs-tag`) follow the project's kebab-case, feature-namespaced convention. Confirmed against the full id inventory (PairScreen uses `pair-*`/`offer-*`/`answer-*`, PhoneApp uses `phone-*`/`motion-*`, CalibrateScreen uses `calibrate-*`). Good.

**N4 — `<video>` without explicit width/height** is fine; CSS at `App.css:818-823` constrains it and the project has no other size-attribute conventions to follow.

### Test adequacy assessment (vs. QUALITY_GATES.md §"Testing gate")

- "Every new module has at least one test exercising its primary path": **pass**. `tag.ts` (11 tests), `library.updateClipTag` + `getClip` (5 tests), `ClipTagScreen` (5 tests).
- "Test names describe behavior under test, not implementation": **pass** — names like "writes cueId + cueAtMs onto an existing clip", "clamps cueAtMs to durationMs when over (avoids tagging past end of clip)", "closes (via onClose) when the clipId cannot be found".
- "Tests fail if the feature were removed": **pass for pure helpers and library**; **partial for ClipTagScreen** — no test catches B2 (the blob-URL churn on save). After B2 is fixed, S1 closes this gap.
- "Edge cases / error paths tested for risky logic": **pass** — clamping above/below range, NaN/Infinity, missing clipId, prefill, save-persist round-trip. The negative path `updateClipTag` returns null on missing id is covered.

### Verdict

**REQUEST_CHANGES**

Blockers B1 (verify artifact inconsistency), B2 (blob URL churns on save), and B3 (effect refetches on parent re-render) need resolution. B2/B3 are small surgical fixes with corresponding tests; B1 is just rerunning the gate script and overwriting `results.json`. After those, this is clean to land.

But if you want zero accumulated drift, track frame *count* in state and derive ms = `Math.round(frameCount * FRAME_STEP_MS)` on each render.

**N2 — Playwright addition is appropriate, not removable** 
- The user asked whether dropping the testing-library deps would have been cleaner. No — those are the only practical way to test a `.tsx` component under vitest's jsdom env. Conversely, `playwright` as devDep was overdue (already required by 9 verify scripts) — moving it from implicit-via-`npx` to explicit is the right call.

**N3 — data-testid convention compliance**
- All new ids (`clip-tag-loading`, `clip-tag-close`, `clip-tag-video`, `clip-tag-frame-back`, `clip-tag-scrub`, `clip-tag-frame-forward`, `clip-tag-position`, `clip-tag-cue-select`, `clip-tag-save`, `clip-tag-saved`, `clip-tag-open`, `clip-row-actions`, `clip-needs-tag`) follow the project's kebab-case, feature-namespaced convention. Confirmed against the full id inventory (PairScreen uses `pair-*`/`offer-*`/`answer-*`, PhoneApp uses `phone-*`/`motion-*`, CalibrateScreen uses `calibrate-*`). Good.

**N4 — `<video>` without explicit width/height** is fine; CSS at `App.css:818-823` constrains it and the project has no other size-attribute conventions to follow.

### Test adequacy assessment (vs. QUALITY_GATES.md §"Testing gate")

- "Every new module has at least one test exercising its primary path": **pass**. `tag.ts` (11 tests), `library.updateClipTag` + `getClip` (5 tests), `ClipTagScreen` (5 tests).
- "Test names describe behavior under test, not implementation": **pass** — names like "writes cueId + cueAtMs onto an existing clip", "clamps cueAtMs to durationMs when over (avoids tagging past end of clip)", "closes (via onClose) when the clipId cannot be found".
- "Tests fail if the feature were removed": **pass for pure helpers and library**; **partial for ClipTagScreen** — no test catches B2 (the blob-URL churn on save). After B2 is fixed, S1 closes this gap.
- "Edge cases / error paths tested for risky logic": **pass** — clamping above/below range, NaN/Infinity, missing clipId, prefill, save-persist round-trip. The negative path `updateClipTag` returns null on missing id is covered.

### Verdict

**REQUEST_CHANGES**

Blockers B1 (verify artifact inconsistency), B2 (blob URL churns on save), and B3 (effect refetches on parent re-render) need resolution. B2/B3 are small surgical fixes with corresponding tests; B1 is just rerunning the gate script and overwriting `results.json`. After those, this is clean to land.
